subject: MAP: monthly token slicing & fallback plan for Q3 rollout
messages:
From: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@fastretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: FastRetail Legal <legal@fastretail.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: monthly token slicing & fallback plan for Q3 rollout

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency profile and the KV caching demo looked promising. We need to lock down a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so our ops and procurement teams can coordinate the Q3 store rollout. A few constraints from our side:

- We will stagger across regions: 20 stores in July, 60 in August, 120 in September — the token consumption per store varies but we estimate a rough monthly TPM target.
- Procurement needs clear committed monthly token targets (TPM) per month, and a fallback/burst policy if traffic exceeds commitments temporarily.
- Our CFO has asked for a clear discount ladder tied to sustained commit (3/6/12 month tiers).

Can you propose a MAP that:
1) maps monthly TPM to committed tiers,
2) includes a soft-commit/fallback burst allowance for unexpected traffic spikes, and
3) spells out credits or workbacks if we significantly underutilize a committed tier?

Have legal looped in on the contract cadence (cc'd). Ideally we'd get something draft-ready for our procurement review by end of next week (May 14).

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Murphy
VP, AI Product
FastRetail

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, FastRetail Legal <legal@fastretail.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: monthly token slicing & fallback plan for Q3 rollout

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Drafting a practical MAP is exactly what we've been doing for similar rollouts; below is a proposal we can iterate on quickly. High-level summary first, then a short table for the commit/discounts and fallback behavior.

High level
- Proposal: a 6-month rolling MAP that starts July 1 (pilot month July for 20 stores). We propose an initial soft-commit tier with a 15% monthly burst allowance and a path to a firm commit after month 2 if usage is consistent.
- Reasoning: the soft-commit gives you operational safety without forcing premature spend; after two months of sustained utilization we can transition to a firm-tier discount that reduces unit price.

Commit ladder (example)
- Tier A (Soft POC): 25M tokens/month baseline — no volume discount; 15% burst allowed (billed at on-demand rate beyond burst).
- Tier B (Growth): 75M tokens/month baseline — 10% unit discount; 15% burst allowed; if sustained >= 90% usage for 2 full months we can convert to Tier C pricing for next month.
- Tier C (Committed): 200M tokens/month baseline — 18% unit discount; 20% burst allowed; 12-month minimum term available for additional 5% credit.

Fallback & burst mechanics
- Automatic burst: any traffic within burst allowance is accepted and billed at committed unit price. Over-burst is billed at on-demand (higher) rate unless you have purchase order to increase commit.
- Emergency capacity: Redwood will provide up to 2x short-term capacity for up to 48 hours for operational incidents; this is priced at a pre-agreed surge rate and eligible for partial credits if outage is due to Redwood.
- Underutilization: if actual usage is < 60% of committed average for 2 consecutive months, we will offer a one-time credit equal to 30% of the monthly commit difference or allow you to step down one tier with 30 days notice (whichever you prefer).

Next steps / timeline
- I'll attach a MAP worksheet (est. commit slices per month for Jul/Aug/Sep) and a pricing summary. Please review and tell us whether: (a) the burst levels are acceptable, (b) the underutilization credit is reasonable, and (c) your procurement timeline for signing.

I will loop Marissa for the exact pricing matrix and Ben for technical SLO language in the contract. If this looks OK I'll push a formal MAP spreadsheet by EOD.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@fastretail.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, FastRetail Legal <legal@fastretail.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 08:51:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: monthly token slicing & fallback plan for Q3 rollout

Alex/Soojin — attaching a draft MAP workbook and a concise pricing summary. Highlights:

- Line-item pricing per 1M tokens (committed vs on-demand) and how the 10/18/23% tiers map by monthly commit.
- Example monthly slices for your July/Aug/Sept ramp based on your store counts: Jul = 18M tokens, Aug = 65M tokens, Sep = 180M tokens (we used conservative per-store assumptions).
- Underutilization mechanics: we added an option for a seasonal buffer (you can carry forward up to 20% of unused tokens for one adjacent month) in addition to the one-time credit already proposed.

Attachments:
- FastRetail_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx (MAP worksheet, slices by region, contract language snippets)
- pricing_summary_FR-041.pdf (unit prices and example invoice math)

Open items for negotiation:
1) Burst allowance: standard is 15% — we can stretch to 20% for the first two months of your rollout if that helps you avoid operational risk.
2) Firm-commit acceleration: if you hit >=95% utilization for any month we can auto-upgrade your discount one tier the following month (needs procurement sign-off).
3) Escrow for credits vs invoice offsets: finance needs clarity whether credits are applied as invoice offsets or as cash credits; leaning toward invoice offsets to simplify billing.

Please flag anything you want changed; if legal signs off on the invoice-offset approach, we can present a redline by May 13 for your procurement intake.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@fastretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: FastRetail Legal <legal@fastretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: monthly token slicing & fallback plan for Q3 rollout

Soojin/Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook. A few notes from procurement/legal after a quick read:

- The staging numbers look reasonable. We like the 20% short-term burst for first two months (please put that in the MAP worksheet).
- On underutilization: procurement prefers carry-forward tokens for one adjacent month + invoice-offset credits rather than a cash credit — that's acceptable.
- On the auto-upgrade clause (>=95% utilization): legal wants that to be an opt-in checkbox in the MAP rather than automatic. Can you add that option?

Procurement target: receive a signed MAP + SOW by May 21 to hit our PO cutoff for the July pilot. Legal will require: (1) invoice-offset detail in the payment terms, (2) SLOs for token delivery (latency P50/P95) and (3) a short paragraph on our surge handling and notification windows.

If you can send an updated workbook with the 20% first-two-months burst allowance, the opt-in auto-upgrade checkbox, and the invoice-offset language, we can route to procurement for signature.

I'll coordinate internally and aim to get back with a locked PO path by May 14.

Cheers — Alex
Alex Murphy
VP, AI Product
FastRetail
